twoFactor.title: Two-factor sign-in
twoFactor.description: When you sign in with your password, we also ask for a code from an app on your phone. Someone who only knows your password cannot get in.
twoFactor.googleNote: When you sign in with Google, Google asks for the second factor, not us.
twoFactor.on: On since {date}. {count, plural, one {# recovery code} other {# recovery codes}} left.
twoFactor.requiredByCompany: Your company requires the second factor, so it stays on.
twoFactor.requiredByPlatform: As a platform admin you always need the second factor.
twoFactor.startFailed: The setup could not start. Please try again.
twoFactor.setupScan: 1. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, for example Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or your password manager.
twoFactor.setupSave: 2. Save the ten recovery codes somewhere safe. Each one gets you in once if your phone is missing. You only see them now.
twoFactor.setupConfirm: 3. Enter the code the app shows now.
twoFactor.confirmLabel: Code from the app or a recovery code
twoFactor.newCodesShown: Your new recovery codes. The old ones no longer work. You only see these now.
twoFactor.turnedOn: Turned on. All your sessions were ended; sign in again with the code.
twoFactor.turnedOff: Turned off. All your sessions were ended; sign in again.
twoFactor.wrongCode: That code does not match. Use the code the app shows now.
twoFactor.locked: Codes from the app are not accepted right now, after too many wrong codes or because this installation's key changed. Use a recovery code.
twoFactor.tooMany: Too many tries. Please wait a few minutes.

twoFactorRequired.label: Require a second factor for everyone
twoFactorRequired.description: Everyone in this company signs in with their password and a code from an app. Anyone who has not set the app up yet does so at their next sign-in. For sign-ins with Google, Google asks.
twoFactorRequired.turnedOn: From their next sign-in, everyone needs a code from the app.
twoFactorRequired.turnedOff: The second factor is no longer required for everyone.

mcp.title: Connect assistants like Claude or Copilot
mcp.description: A connected assistant reads your NIS 2 walkthrough and fills in fields and registers, with your rights in this company. When you ask, it sends suppliers on your list the security questionnaire. An item is finished only here in the app, and signed only by management.
mcp.signIn: Assistants that sign in through the browser need no key: you sign in and allow access. The key is for all others.
mcp.howTo: How to set up Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Copilot Studio
mcp.readsRecords: Because you may export the company's records and your admin lets assistants read them, the assistant can also read them, exactly as the export holds them.
mcp.created: Your key, valid for 90 days. It is shown only now.
mcp.replaceNote: A new key ends the previous key; assistants that signed in stay connected. Disconnecting all ends both.

connections.title: Connected
connections.loadFailed: The connected assistants could not be loaded. Reload the page.

mcp.failed: That did not work. Please try again.
mcp.companyChanged: You opened another company in a different tab. Reload this page to connect in the company you have open.
mcp.off: Your company has not allowed AI assistants. An admin turns them on above.
mcp.offAdmin: Assistants are off for this company. Turn them on above to connect one.

switch.label: Allow AI assistants for this company
switch.description: When on, people in this company may connect their own assistant, which then reads and fills in the walkthrough with the company's data and can send suppliers on the list the security questionnaire. Turning it off ends every connected assistant.
switch.turnedOff: AI assistants are off. Every connection has ended.

recordsSwitch.label: Let assistants read the company's records
recordsSwitch.description: When on, the assistant of someone who may export (admins, reviewers, legal reviewers, management) can read all of the company's records as the export holds them: registers, incidents, training participants and contact persons. Everyone else's assistant reads only the walkthrough. Turning it off stops the next read.
recordsSwitch.turnedOn: Assistants of people who may export can read the records.
recordsSwitch.turnedOff: Assistants no longer read the records.

mcp.locked: An assistant works in the NIS 2 walkthrough, which is not unlocked for your account yet. Until it is, an assistant can read and fill in nothing.
mcp.copyFailed: Copying did not work. Select the key in the field and copy it yourself.
mcp.reauth: An assistant stays connected even after you sign out, so connecting one needs a sign-in from the last {minutes} minutes.

connect.title: Connect an assistant
connect.asks: {client} wants to access the NIS 2 walkthrough of {company}.
connect.may: It reads the walkthrough, fills in fields and registers and sends suppliers on your list the security questionnaire, as {person} and with your rights.
connect.mayNot: It finishes no item, decides nothing and signs nothing. That stays here in the app.
connect.selfNamed: The name “{client}” is the one the assistant gives itself.
connect.onlyYou: Allow only if you started this connection yourself just now.
connect.expired: This request has expired or is not valid. Start the connection again in the assistant.
connect.disconnectHint: You can disconnect at any time in Settings.
connect.failed: That did not work. Please try again.
connect.companyChanged: You opened another company in a different tab. Reload this page to connect in the company you have open.
connect.off: This company's admin has not allowed AI assistants, so none can be connected. Ask your admin, or decline.
connect.offAdmin: AI assistants are off for this company. Turn them on here to connect this one. Everyone in the company can then connect their own.
connect.setupFirst: An AI assistant asked to connect to your company. Set up your company first: once it is saved, this page asks you whether to allow the assistant. If the request has run out by then, start the sign-in in the assistant again.
